options.text: What's the biggest battle you've been in?
Tell me about a battle you'll never forget.
Seen much real fighting?
What was your first battle like?
Ever been through a proper siege?
What's the hardest fight you've ever won?
Tell me about a fight your side lost.
What does a battle actually feel like?
Any battle stories worth a listen?
Were you at any of the engagements people sing about?
What's the longest you've fought without rest?
Tell me about the worst charge you ever faced.
How did you survive your first real combat?
Which fight still keeps you up at night?
What's the closest you've come to dying?
Ever have a really near miss?
Any brushes with death lately?
What's the luckiest escape you've ever had?
Ever been left for dead?
Ever think your number was up?
How many lives have you burned through, you reckon?
What saved you when nothing should have?
Ever been buried, trapped, cornered — that sort of thing?
Tell me about a time you almost didn't make it.
Have you lost people close to you?
Tell me about a friend who didn't make it.
How do your people honor the dead?
Who do you miss the most?
Do you ever visit the graves?
What happens to a fallen comrade's belongings?
Is it true every soldier carries a name they can't say aloud?
How do you keep going after losing friends?
Was there someone who saved you and paid for it?
Do you remember all of them?
What do you actually do all day out here?
Doesn't the waiting drive you mad?
What's garrison life really like?
How do you pass the slow hours?
Is soldiering mostly boredom, like they say?
Any games you play to kill time?
What's the dullest posting you've ever pulled?
What's the strangest hobby in your camp?
Why did you join up?
Did you choose this life, or did it choose you?
What made you enlist?
Would you sign on again, knowing what you know now?
Was joining a family tradition?
Did they promise you anything to sign?
How old were you when you took the oath?
What did your family say when you joined?
Ever regret enlisting?
What do you miss most from home?
Where's home for you?
Do you get letters from home?
Do you dream about home much?
Anyone waiting for you back there?
How long since you've been home?
What does home smell like? Mine's woodsmoke.
Tell me about the place you grew up.
If you could be anywhere else right now, where?
What's the worst night you've ever had out here?
Everyone has one terrible story. What's yours?
What was your darkest hour?
Ever have a night where everything went wrong at once?
What came closest to breaking you?
Tell me something the war did to you that you didn't expect.
What still gives you nightmares?
When were you last truly afraid?
What's the best meal you've had in service?
How's the food in your outfit, honestly?
What passes for a feast around here?
Weirdest thing you've ever eaten in the field?
Who's the best cook in your camp?
What would you trade a day's pay to eat right now?
Are the rations any good, or do you all just pretend?
Are soldiers really as superstitious as they say?
Got a lucky charm on you?
Any rituals before a fight?
What's considered bad luck around here?
Do you believe in omens?
Anything you'd never do before a battle?
What's the strangest belief in your unit?
Is there something you always carry with you?
What do you make of your commanders?
Is your commander any good?
Do you trust the people giving the orders?
Who's the best officer you've served under?
Ever been given an order you hated?
What makes a good commander, in your book?
Do the higher-ups know what it's like down here?
Any leaders worth following into the dark?
What will you do when the war's over?
Got any dreams for after all this?
Where do you see yourself in ten years?
What's the first thing you'll do when peace comes?
Do you ever think about life after soldiering?
Will you stay a soldier when it ends?
What are you fighting for, at the end of the day?
If peace came tomorrow, what would you do with it?
What kind of life do you want after this?
What's the cleverest operation you've ever run?
Tell me about a campaign from the commander's chair.
What's the hardest order you've ever given?
How do you actually plan a battle?
What do they never teach about command?
Tell me about a plan that worked perfectly.
Tell me about a plan that fell apart.
Know any ghost stories?
It's the right kind of dark for a frightening tale.
Ever seen something out here you couldn't explain?
Do the dead ever walk this ground?
What's the eeriest thing that's happened on your watch?
Any haunted places near here?
Tell me something that'll keep me up tonight.
That fight just now — are you alright?
I caught the tail end of that skirmish. What happened?
Your hands are shaking. Rough one?
How do you come down after a fight like that?
Fresh marks on the ground out there. Close one?
That was quite a scrap. Tell me everything.
Still upright after that? Impressive.
Come on, surely you've got one story for me.
Even enemies swap stories sometimes. Got one?
Tell me a story. Any story.
What happens to people your side takes against?
Got any tales about folk who crossed you?
Tell me a story with a moral, then.
Humor me with one tale and I'll leave you be.
What do your people do with their enemies, exactly?
Any advice for someone on your bad side?
Tell me about the last person who stood right here.
What's the worst your side has done to someone like me?
If I keep coming around, how does that story end?
You can tell me the real version. I keep secrets.
What's something you've never told your squad?
Between us — what are you most afraid of?
Tell me something true. Not the campfire version.
What do you think about on watch, honestly?
Who were you before the war?
Do you ever doubt all this?
What's the kindest thing you've seen in this war?
What's your real story? Not the one you tell recruits.
Have you ever disobeyed an order for someone?
What would your mother make of who you've become?
Is there anything you'd take back, if you could?
How did you get that scar?
That's quite a mark. What's the story behind it?
Every scar has a tale. Pick one.
Which of your scars has the best story?
Which wound hurt worst to earn?
Any scars you're actually proud of?
Any scars from something embarrassing? Be honest.
Show me a scar and I'll show you mine.
Thanks for the stories. I'd best move on.
That's enough war for one day. Goodbye.
I've heard all I can carry. Take care.
I shouldn't have asked. Forget I did.
Save the rest for next time.
It's getting late. I'll go.

negative: You want battle stories? Ask your conscience. It was there for some of ours.
Our battles are lists of names. You've added to the lists. No stories for you.
neutral: Ridge 9. Three days, no sleep, spades and teeth. We kept the ridge. It kept forty of us.
They came at dawn, all brass and banners. By noon the banners were bandages. We held.
A battle is loud boredom. Hours of nothing, then ninety seconds you never stop hearing.
positive: Sit. The marsh assault — nobody tells it right but me, because I was the one face-down in it.
We once held a farmhouse with six men and a stubborn goat. The goat got a medal. Sort of.
I'll tell you about the night charge. Slowly. It deserves a slow telling.

negative: After-action reports aren't entertainment for people with your record.
Our engagements are filed, not performed. Access denied.
neutral: Hill 12: textbook envelopment until rain killed visibility. Then knives and nerve. We adapted.
One bridge, two companies, nine hours. We rehearsed it forty times. The fight only counted once.
Combat is checklists until it isn't. The gap between is where soldiers are made.
positive: Off the record: the relief of Outpost 4. Fourteen of us, one signal mirror, perfect timing. My proudest shift.
The canal crossing, friend. Doctrine failed at minute ten. Sergeant Vale improvised. We drill her improvisation now.
I'll walk you through the quarry ambush sometime. Bring something to take notes with. It's that good.

negative: Our battles are not stories. They are debts being repaid. Yours accrues.
The lion does not narrate the hunt to the prey.
neutral: There was a caravan of soldiers, proud as noon. The desert opened, then closed. We were the closing.
We fought at the dry river. They arrived a thousand; they left a rumor.
Battles? We prefer arithmetic done in advance. The fighting is only the receipt.
positive: Come close. The night of the red moon — three of us, a hundred of them, and the dune that walked. All true. Mostly.
I will tell you of the well that swallowed an army's courage. It cost me a scar and a cousin, so listen well.
For you, the story of the whistling pass. When I finish you will hear it in every wind.

negative: Closest I came to dying? Might be right now, depending how this chat goes.
I survive things. Remember that on your way out.
neutral: A cave-in buried me once. The line dug me out because I still owed Pyotr money. Debt saves lives.
An arrow parted my hair at the wire. The barber's been out of work since.
Fell through ice hauling timber. The cold spat me back. Even the cold has quotas.
positive: Friend, I've been dead twice on paper. The clerk apologizes every time we meet.
A blade this close. THIS close. My collar button died a hero.
The trench collapsed on me and I dreamed of my grandmother's stove. Then the shovels came. I still hate stoves.

negative: My close calls are logged. So is the cause of the latest ones. Care to guess?
I don't discuss vulnerabilities with threats.
neutral: Rope gave out on the cliff descent. Second anchor held. That's why doctrine says two of everything.
A spear took my pack off my shoulders instead of my head. I now walk half a step to the left, always.
The signal tower took lightning while I was on it. I finished the transmission first. Priorities.
positive: Between us: I froze once. Whole squad passed me on the ladder. Sergeant covered for me. I owe her my career.
A trap under the floorboards. I heard the click and just... waited. Longest four seconds of my life, friend.
Ambush at the ford — went under twice with full kit. Kept the ledger dry, though. Quartermaster still toasts me.

negative: The scorpion under my pillow was tame compared to present company.
I have survived storms, sieges, and betrayals. You are none of the three. Yet.
neutral: A sandstorm ate my patrol's tracks and nearly ate me. I walked home by the taste of the wind.
Once I drank from the wrong well. Three days of fever, one very honest conversation with the moon.
A blade found my ribs at the pass. My ribs, praise them, argued back.
positive: Friend, I fell into a slot canyon at midnight and landed on the one ledge in a hundred feet. The desert keeps favorites.
I hid from a search party inside a camel's shadow for an hour. The camel never told. Camels are honorable.
A viper chose my boot for a house. We negotiated. I went barefoot; the boot went to the viper. Fair terms.

negative: Our dead have names and your face sits next to some of them. Ask me nothing about the fallen.
You want to hear about our dead? Buy a shovel. Help dig for the next ones.
neutral: We don't say 'lost'. Nothing's lost. They're in the line still, just very quiet.
Marta carried the cook pot and the jokes. The pot survived. Some trades the war forces on you.
We carve the names on the duckboards. You walk on them. They'd like that — still useful.
positive: I'll tell you about Osip. Loudest laugh, worst singer, best friend. The line is quieter and worse fed without him.
My brother's in the eastern field, third row. I tell him the soup news weekly. He always liked the soup news.
We drink the first cup to them, always. Tonight you can hold a cup too, friend.

negative: Casualty records are sealed. Especially from those who authored entries.
You don't get to mourn ours. That privilege is earned in the opposite direction.
neutral: We read the roll on the first of each month. Every name, full rank, no abbreviations. It takes as long as it takes.
Specialist Iri held the relay alone for six hours. The relay stands. We maintain it like a grave, because it is one.
Losses are processed by procedure. Grief is processed off duty. Both get done, civilian.
positive: Her name was Corporal Denn. She checked everyone's knots twice. Mine held on the cliff because of her. Hers didn't.
My bunkmate logged the weather every dawn, even under attack. I keep the habit now. It's him I'm writing down, really.
We lost Lieutenant Maro covering a withdrawal she ordered against orders. Court papers and a medal came the same week.

negative: Our dead are seeds in the sand. Do not ask what grows from them. You may find out.
Name our fallen? Their names are being saved for a better listener.
neutral: We do not bury our dead. The desert adopts them. It is a larger family than yours.
My cousin Naila walks ahead of every patrol now, in her way. The desert lets the dead keep working.
For each one taken, we plant a stone in a dry place. There are gardens of them now. Quiet gardens.
positive: I will say his name because you ask kindly: Tarek. He taught me to read wind. Every dawn I read it and he is there.
My sister fell at the salt flats. On still nights the salt shines like her laugh. I patrol there gladly.
We tell the dead the news at the fire's last ember. Stay tonight, friend, and you may tell them something too.

negative: Boredom? With you around, the watch stays interesting. Not a compliment.
Dull days are for people without your history. Ours end.
neutral: Garrison life is soup, mud, cards, mud, inspection, mud. The mud rotates.
We rate the days by boot-dryness. Today is a two. Yesterday was a one. Exciting times.
Boredom is the good stuff. Boredom means the wire held and nobody's crying.
positive: Want the truth, friend? I've memorized every knot in that beam. I've named six of them.
We hold lice races. My champion is called General. Undefeated, like all generals — on paper.
The card deck's down to 41 cards. We play anyway. New rules every week. It's basically culture now.

negative: Quiet shifts would be quieter without flagged persons making conversation.
Downtime is for maintenance, not for entertaining you.
neutral: Garrison rhythm: inspect, drill, log, rotate. Repetition is the point. Sharp edges are made by repetition.
Boredom is a readiness state. We train it like everything else.
A slow watch means the deterrence is working. I can live with slow.
positive: Confession, friend: I alphabetize the supply shelves for fun now. Twice. By two different systems.
We run signal-flag poetry contests off shift. Command pretends not to know. Command took second place last month.
I've counted the fence posts. 214. If it's ever 213, I'll be the fastest-moving bored man alive.

negative: You mistake stillness for boredom. The trap is also still.
Our quiet is occupied. Mostly with accounts like yours.
neutral: The desert has no boring days, only slow ones. Slow is where the thinking gets done.
We watch. Watching looks like idleness the way a bowstring looks like rope.
Garrison? Our garrison is the horizon. It never needs sweeping and never lets you rest.
positive: Friend, I have spent nine days watching one pass. I know every lizard by temperament now. Rashid is the moody one.
In the slow weeks we hold poetry duels. I lost to my aunt last month. The wound is deep.
I taught a raven three words this season. All complaints. He fits right in.

negative: Why I enlisted is mine. Why I stay gets clearer every time you visit.
I joined to protect people from types like you turned out to be.
neutral: The line came through my village going one direction. Easier to join than to be behind it.
Three brothers, one farm. The arithmetic sent me here. Someone digs, someone inherits.
The recruiter promised boots and bread. He was half right. I forget which half.
positive: Truth? A girl. She married a baker instead. The baker's dead, the bakery's ash. The line goes on. So do I.
My mother said: better a shovel in the line than a plow behind it. Mothers know.
I joined for the winter coat, friend. Fourteen years ago. It's a good coat.

negative: My reasons for service are on file. Your reasons for asking concern me more.
I serve so people like you meet people like me at a wall instead of a village. Next question.
neutral: Scholarship program. Signals training in exchange for service years. The math held up.
My town flooded twice with no plan. Aegis had a plan. I wanted to be part of something that plans.
Aptitude testing routed me here. The system knew me better than I did. It usually does.
positive: Honestly? I saw a formation drill at fourteen. All that order in a broken world. I never wanted anything else.
My father served, and his mother before him. The uniform's practically a family heirloom with sleeves.
I enlisted angry, friend. The discipline gave the anger somewhere useful to live. Saved my life, probably.

negative: Why does the thorn grow on the fruit tree? Ask the ones who kept picking.
I was recruited by consequences. Some of them resembled you.
neutral: No one enlists in the desert. The desert enlists you, then negotiates.
My village needed eyes on the horizon. I had eyes. It is not more complicated.
The sand took my herd in one storm. The brotherhood shares water. Simple as thirst.
positive: My grandmother traded a stranger shade for water once. That stranger was Sarab. We have been kin since.
I joined for my brother, who joined for his friend, who joined for a girl. Wars run on such strings, friend.
As a boy I watched raiders take our well. Sarab took it back by dawn. I followed them out of gratitude and never stopped.

negative: What do I miss? Days before I knew your name.
Home talk is for friends. We are colleagues in mutual suspicion at best.
neutral: I miss floors. Real floors. Wood, dry, flat. You people with floors don't know your wealth.
The smell of my mother's rye bread. The mud has a smell too. It is not rye bread.
Bathhouses. A proper steam. First thing after the war: I boil myself for a week.
positive: My daughter's terrible violin, friend. Awful sound. I'd give a month's rations to hear it out of tune again.
The dog. I miss the dog most. Don't tell my wife the order I said that in.
Sunday pierogi and arguments about nothing. We argue here too, but the stakes ruin it.

negative: Personal details are not shared. Miss whatever you like on my behalf.
Home is what I keep people like you away from. That's all you get.
neutral: Hot water on demand. You stop noticing marvels until you're rationing them.
Streetlights. A lit street with no tactical significance. Just light, for walking.
My own bed and exactly zero snoring bunkmates. The brochure never mentioned snoring.
positive: My sister's kids, friend. They think my signal mirror is magic. I let them. It is, a little.
There's a bakery on Copper Street that opens at five. I've been on watch at five for years. The nose remembers.
Rain on a roof I'm not responsible for defending. That specific sound. I'd trade a promotion for a night of it.

negative: What I miss was taken. Some of the taking had faces like yours.
The homesick tell their wells, not their watchers.
neutral: I miss the sea I have never seen. The desert teaches you to miss forward as well as back.
My mother's courtyard had a fig tree. I measure all shade against it. All shade loses.
The sound of many cousins arguing over one pot. Silence is useful, but it is not that.
positive: Friend, I miss being unimportant. A boy with a stick and a goat and no name worth watching. Sweet, unimportant days.
My wife sings to the bread so it rises. Two years since I heard fresh bread. Ration bread is sung to by no one.
The night market at home — lamps, dates, ten liars telling one story. When the war ends, I will be the eleventh.

negative: My worst night made me patient. You are spending that patience.
The worst nights make lists. I told you we count. That is all I will say.
neutral: The night the river froze wrong. We heard the ice all night. Not everything we heard was ice.
Flood in the trenches, winter of the long push. We held the wire till dawn. Some sat down in it. Don't sit.
Worst night was quiet. All quiet. Then the signal fire, and by morning the platoon was half a platoon.
positive: The night we lost the forward sap. I held Osip's hand and lied about the medic. He knew. He let me lie. That was kindness.
I'll tell you mine if you never repeat it: I cried into a ration tin so the recruits wouldn't hear. It rained anyway.
Second winter. We burned the chess set for warmth. Grown men mourned a wooden horse. I include battles when I rank it.

negative: My worst night involved counting our dead. Some ledgers you've seen from the other side.
Nights like that are classified. So is my patience tonight.
neutral: Comms blackout, storm, and a breach alarm all in one watch. Procedure held. Barely. We rewrote it after.
The night the relay chain failed, every post was an island. You learn what silence costs when it's sold by the hour.
We lost a supply column to a washed-out road. No enemy involved. The worst nights are often just weather and arithmetic.
positive: Between us: the retreat from the north wall. I gave a wrong grid under pressure. Two hours to fix. I re-check everything now.
Holding a dying man's hand while reciting the evac checklist — the only calm I had to offer. It worked. For me, I mean.
The flood watch, year two. We saved the equipment first. Doctrine said to. I still hear the man doctrine didn't save.

negative: My worst night is patient. It waits in me. Do not knock on that door.
Some nights are knives that keep their sheaths. Be glad this is one.
neutral: The night of the black wind. We tied ourselves to stones. Not everyone knots well. The desert kept its tax.
A guide sold our route once. The night that followed taught us new prices for trust.
The wells went bitter one summer night — all of them, together. Nature does not do that. We learned who could.
positive: For you: the night my brother did not come back from the dune line. I still leave the tent flap loose. Habits of hope, friend.
The worst night had no enemy. Fever in the camp, me with two hands and forty thirsty. I ration my mercy better now.
Once I sat all night with a dying rival, trading stories till dawn took him. Worst night. Best stories. The desert is like that.

negative: The best meals are eaten with people we trust. So: nothing to report.
Why, planning to poison one? The soup guards itself.
neutral: A potato. Whole, unshared, hot. Year one, after the bridge. Emperors have eaten worse and bragged more.
Horse sausage after the thaw. Ask no questions of the sausage. The sausage earned respect.
Captured enemy rations once. Excellent tin. Whoever supplies them, they fight for good biscuits.
positive: Friend, once the cook cried into the soup and it was the best seasoning all winter. We never told him why we asked for more.
My best meal was half a dumpling. Marta had the other half. It's the company that cooks, you understand.
New Year, year three. Real butter appeared. Nobody asked from where. The quartermaster smiled for a week. A WEEK.

negative: Meal records are logistics data. Denied, with seasoning.
I don't break bread with flagged persons, even in conversation.
neutral: Field ration type C, heated correctly for once. Preparation matters more than ingredients. Kitchen doctrine.
The mess hall on inspection day. Coincidence? Nothing in Aegis is coincidence, including the gravy.
A hot meal delivered on time under attack is a logistics miracle. I've had three. I remember each convoy's number.
positive: Winter solstice, the cooks did a night feast on the wall. Steam in the torchlight, the watch singing quiet. Best duty meal ever.
My sergeant's unauthorized stew. The recipe is a court-martial waiting to happen. Worth it. I said what I said, friend.
After the quarry op, someone's mother had sent honey cakes. Eight soldiers, one tin, full ceremony. We ate like a treaty was signed.

negative: You ask about our table with your history? Bold. The answer is: guarded.
The best meal is one eaten without watching the door. With you nearby, no such meal exists.
neutral: Dates, salt bread, and shade at the right hour. The desert's whole cookbook is timing.
Rain-water tea after the long dry. Water you have waited months for has a taste money never buys.
A hare, a fire, a pass held safely behind us. Plain food after unplain work is the recipe.
positive: My aunt's lamb with seven spices, eaten the night before my first patrol. I have marched four years on that memory, friend.
A stranger once split his last figs with my patrol, not knowing us. His flock has been the safest in the desert since.
Festival of the first star — the whole camp cooks, every pot is everyone's. Taste one spoon of that and you understand us.

negative: I believe unlucky people bring their luck with them. It's why I'm watching you.
Superstition? Counting is my superstition. Yours is coming out even. It doesn't.
neutral: Never whistle in the trench. The trench whistles back. This is fact, not superstition.
Third flame is bad luck — light two pipes, then snuff it and dig a hole for it. Don't ask. Dig.
New boots before a push? Someone else will wear them after. Everyone patches instead.
positive: I keep a button from my first coat, friend. Fourteen years, never lost a fight while it's sewn on. It stays sewn.
We salute the crows. They skipped our trench in the bad winter. Respect is owed. The crows know.
Our stove has a name and a temper. You feed it the first knuckle of every loaf or the week goes wrong. House rules.

negative: Aegis doesn't do superstition. We do risk assessment. You assess poorly.
The only omen I track is your presence. The correlation's been bad.
neutral: Officially, none. Unofficially, nobody says a patrol is 'routine' out loud. Nobody. Twice was enough.
We don't repaint post 13. It's fine as it is. It will stay as it is. Next topic.
Checklists are our ritual. The difference between ritual and procedure is whether it works. Ours works.
positive: Between us: I tap the gate twice going out, once coming in. Every soldier does something. Mine's just quieter than most.
There's a lucky signal flag — the old torn one. It flew through the worst siege we've had. It retires when I do, friend.
My squad won't rotate without saying 'see you at debrief'. Not goodbye. Never goodbye. Words are load-bearing, it turns out.

negative: We have one superstition: those who spill guest-blood carry a wind behind them. Feel your neck? That.
Ask instead what the omens say about you. No — you would not sleep.
neutral: Never count your water out loud. The sun hears. The sun is greedy.
A snake crossing right to left blesses the journey. Left to right, camp early and check your boots twice.
We do not speak the names of sandstorms. Named things visit.
positive: I carry sand from my birth-dune in a pouch, friend. When I cannot sleep, I hold it and I am a boy with a goat again.
Pour the first drop of tea to the ground, always. The desert drinks first. It has never let me down when paid on time.
My grandmother swore the stars rearrange for the honest. I have checked, friend. Some nights, for some people, they do.

negative: My opinion of command is my business. My opinion of you is public record.
You'd like us divided from our officers, wouldn't you. Dig elsewhere.
neutral: The colonel counts like we count. That's all we ask of the high seats. He counts honestly.
Officers come in two kinds: ones who've dug and ones who point. Ours mostly dug. You can tell by the shoulders.
Command is far away. The sergeant is near. We follow the near thing. It has kept us alive.
positive: Our captain once carried a wounded man's pack for nine miles and filed it as 'training'. That's the whole review, friend.
The old major shares his tobacco when the count comes back bad. Small thing. It is not a small thing.
I'd complain about command like any soldier, but ours eats last. Hard to sharpen a knife for a man who eats last.

negative: Chain-of-command assessments are internal. Interest in them from you reads as reconnaissance.
You want gossip about my officers? File a request. It will be denied with full courtesy.
neutral: Command is competent. That sounds cold. In a war, 'competent' is the highest compliment with witnesses.
Our commander reads every after-action to the last line. Decisions improve when someone actually reads. They read.
Orders arrive clear, resupply arrives on time. I don't need to love the chain. I need it to hold. It holds.
positive: Commander Ashe once halted a whole operation over one bad weather report. Career risk against forty lives. We remember.
My lieutenant asks 'what am I missing?' at every briefing. Out loud. In front of everyone. That habit has saved us twice.
Between us, the sector chief plays terrible cards and pays her losses instantly. You learn a lot about command from that.

negative: You ask who leads us. The wind asked the dune the same. It is still asking.
Our leaders' names are wells we do not show strangers. Especially thirsty ones.
neutral: We follow the one who reads the desert best that season. Titles are for people with paper to spare.
Our elders lead by asking questions until the answer is obvious. Slow. Annoying. Correct.
Command with us is a loose rein. The desert punishes tight ones.
positive: Old Yusra has led us through nine dry years. She speaks little. When she points, water is there. Every time, friend.
My captain once walked us AROUND a winnable fight. 'We are not here to win fights,' he said, 'but to win afterwards.'
The one who leads my band carried me on his back across the glass flats. I would follow him into the noon sun. I have.

negative: After the war I'll have time for old accounts. Yours is bookmarked.
Dreams are rationed too. None to spare for this conversation.
neutral: After? A floor, a stove, a door that locks from the inside. I keep my ambitions load-bearing.
They say the land will need rebuilding. Good. We know how to dig. We'll dig gardens for a change.
First: sleep for a month. Second: eat something with a color. Third — there's no third. Two is plenty.
positive: Friend, I'm going to grow potatoes and complain about small things. SMALL things. A leaky bucket. I dream of a leaky bucket.
Me and Pyotr are opening a bathhouse. He can't build and I can't count money. It will be glorious or it will be a story.
I'll teach my daughter to fish where the river isn't a border. Same river, you understand. Just no longer a border.

negative: Post-war planning is above your clearance and beneath my patience.
After the war there will still be walls and lists. Mind which side of both you're on.
neutral: The service will need surveyors, signalers, planners. Peace is a logistics problem too. I'll have work.
Retrain, most likely. The discipline transfers. Aegis people run half the granaries and every decent bridge crew already.
A pension, a workshop, and no night watches. Modest objectives, achievable timeline.
positive: Honestly, friend? I want to teach. Signals school. Hand the kids everything the war taught me, minus the worst of it.
There's a lighthouse posting on the coast. One keeper, big lamp, no tactical anything. I've already applied. Twice.
I'm going to marry the baker on Copper Street, if the war ever lets me finish the sentence I started in that shop.

negative: After the war, the desert remains, and so do its memories. You are in them.
My dreams are not for sale, least of all to buyers of our misfortune.
neutral: After the war we do what sand does after wind: settle, hold what we hold, wait for the next wind.
There will be trade routes again. We know every pass. Perhaps the passes will finally pay in coin instead of blood.
The desert has no 'after'. Only 'meanwhile'. We are good at meanwhile.
positive: I will plant a fig tree in my mother's courtyard, friend, and argue with my cousins about nothing until arguing is a feast.
When it ends, I will guide travelers instead of hunting them. Same skills. Better tips. Fewer regrets.
There is a girl in the northern oasis who keeps bees. After the war I intend to know a great deal more about bees.

negative: Strategy talk with you? I'd sooner publish our maps in the town square.
An officer's stories are half doctrine. You've earned access to neither half.
neutral: The southern salient, two winters back. We traded ground for time, then charged them rent on the ground. Attrition is a landlord.
Strategy at our level: know your losses in advance, then make the enemy exceed theirs. It reads cold. It is.
I once ordered a retreat that looked like a rout on purpose. The pursuit met our reserve. Appearances are ammunition.
positive: Sit, friend — the encirclement at Kraev Marsh. My best work and my worst month, and I'll tell you why they're the same story.
I'll teach you the one rule they leave out of manuals: plan for your soldiers' fear as carefully as the enemy's strength.
The bridge feint, in full, since you ask well: it cost three carts of turnips and won a valley. Best turnips ever spent.

negative: Operational art is not shared with liabilities. That term is in your file, by the way.
You're asking a commander to narrate doctrine to a flagged civilian. Admire the nerve. Decline the request.
neutral: Campaign design is tempo control: act faster than the enemy decides. Everything else is footnotes with casualties.
The eastern pocket taught us to plan the retreat before the advance. Ugly lesson, elegant doctrine.
I rehearse each operation backwards from the worst outcome. Morbid, effective. The staff hates and thanks me.
positive: The coastal deception, friend — three phantom battalions built from lanterns, dust, and a bored drum corps. Still proud.
I'll share the ridge campaign, since you listen properly. We won it in the supply ledgers a month before the first arrow.
A real lesson: I once won a sector by sending the enemy commander accurate weather reports. Trust is also terrain.

negative: You ask the falcon to explain the dive while you're in the field below. No.
Our strategies are wells. Shown only to those who will not spit.
neutral: Strategy is choosing which fights evaporate before they happen. The unfought battle costs nothing and teaches fear.
We won the pass campaign by moving wells. No map shows it. The maps' silence was the victory.
The desert war is a war of appointments. We simply decline the ones we would lose.
positive: Come, listener. The year of the two moons — we let an army chase seventeen of us in circles until it drank itself hollow.
I will teach you our oldest doctrine, friend: the dune wins not by striking but by being everywhere the foot falls.
My finest season: we defeated a siege with rumors, three drums, and patience. The drums were the extravagance.

negative: The dead walk the wire some nights. Ours know your face. Sleep well.
Ghost stories? You bring your own. They follow you around here.
neutral: Some nights the picket hears digging past the wire. Old digging. We do not investigate. It's someone's shift, not ours.
There's a stretch of trench nobody sleeps in. It's warmer than the rest. That is exactly the problem.
In the flooded sector you can hear roll call on still nights. Old names. Nobody answers. You don't answer either.
positive: Come close, friend. The Grey Sapper — he patches wire on the worst nights. Torn gloves by morning, and none were issued.
Once, in white fog, a column marched past our post in perfect step. No mud sound. Old uniforms. We saluted. What else?
The stove in the old dugout lights itself some midnights. We leave tobacco on it now. The stove has earned tobacco.

negative: Night visits from you interest our sentries more than any ghost.
The only haunting in this sector is your record. It follows you closer than any spirit.
neutral: Relay 7 sends at three past midnight some nights. Dead channel, retired code. We log it and do not reply. Logging is enough.
An extra man shows in the night count sometimes. Always the far rank, always gone by lamplight. The count holds anyway.
Official position: there are no ghosts. The unofficial position is on watch at tower four and won't work alone.
positive: A lamp signals from the drowned outpost on foggy nights. Correct code, retired code. We answer 'stand down'. It rests then.
The stairwell in the old tower counts one extra footstep after you stop. Always one. Polite, punctual. Very Aegis, honestly.
My first post had a sentry everyone met and no one had enlisted. Gave excellent warnings. HQ marked the file 'retain'.

negative: The desert dead are patient and partisan. Guess whose side they take.
At night the sand repeats what it has swallowed. Your name comes up.
neutral: There is a caravan that crosses the flats with no tracks and no thirst. Trade nothing to it. Keep your name in your mouth.
Some dunes sing. One dune answers. We do not camp at the one that answers.
Lights walk the wadi on moonless nights. Old lanterns look for old owners. Let them look. Do not be findable.
positive: Sit close, friend. On such nights the Pale Herdsman crosses, counting flocks no living eye sees. Greet him. Water stays sweet.
My grandmother traded a song to the ghost caravan for a skin that never empties. She cannot recall that song now. Fair, she says.
I slept in a ruin once and woke with my boots mended and a stranger's prayer beads in my hand. I keep them oiled. Debts accrue.

negative: Fresh from a fight and straight to chatting with me. My hands are still deciding.
Blood's up. Bad time to be on my list. You're on my list.
neutral: Just now? We held. That's the whole story until my ears stop ringing.
Ask me tomorrow. Today the hands shake and the count isn't final.
The mud's still settling. So am I. Short version: they came, they left fewer.
positive: HA! Did you see? The wire held, the line held, and Pyotr fell in the latrine mid-charge. We lived AND we got a comedy.
Feel that, friend? Still shaking. The first hour after is the most alive a man gets. Then you find the samovar and go mortal.
We just held them with shovels and spite. SHOVELS. I love this stupid unbreakable line, friend. Have a biscuit.

negative: Post-engagement protocol is in effect and you are a known variable. Give me distance.
We just took casualties and your file is your file. Walk away now.
neutral: Contact resolved. Adrenaline is a resource; I'm spending mine on inventory. Talk fast.
The engagement's over, the sweep's not. Debrief in an hour. You get one minute.
Situation contained. Heart rate pending. Standard interval.
positive: Still buzzing, friend. Textbook response, zero friendly losses — the drills paid the whole bill today. THIS is why we rehearse.
You should've seen second squad's flanking work just now. Art. I'd frame it if you could frame a maneuver.
We just turned an ambush inside out in ninety seconds. I'll be insufferable about it for a week. Starting now, with you.

negative: The blade is just wiped and you approach. Courage and foolishness pour from one jug.
We have just fed the sand. It stays hungry. Step back from the edge of that.
neutral: It is done. The wind is already smoothing the marks. Give me a moment to be smoothed as well.
The fight was brief. The stillness after is where we live. You are inside it.
Do not ask for the tale while the dust hangs. Stories need settled dust.
positive: Ha — feel my hand, friend. Steady as stone. It lies. Inside, drums.
We struck like the proverb: the viper is a rumor until it is a fact. Just now we were a fact. Sit, the tea is earned today.
They walked into our shadow just now, whole and confident. They left neither. Tonight the camp sings quietly. You may listen.

negative: Story? Fine. A man kept visiting a trench he'd wronged. One day the trench was closer than he thought. Short story.
Once there was a clever one who thought counting was a bluff. The count is never a bluff. The end.
There was a fox that liked our wire. Bold fox. Beautiful coat. The coat's on the sergeant's bunk now.
neutral: A recruit skipped the duckboards to save ten steps. The mud taught him about shortcuts. We pulled him out — mostly laughing.
One winter a man traded his shovel for extra bread. Rich for a week, digging with a spoon by spring. Keep the shovel.
positive: A friendly warning story: never accept 'quiet sector' as a compliment. Quiet is a debt with interest, friend.
We had a lucky man once. Truly lucky. He relaxed. The lesson isn't about luck, friend. It's about relaxing.

negative: Here's one: an unauthorized person kept probing a perimeter's patience. The patience was policy. Policy ran out.
A civilian once mistook courtesy for tolerance. The distinction is in his file now. Closed file.
We tracked a poacher on the wire for a season. He thought unnoticed meant unwatched. The season ended.
neutral: Cautionary tale from the manual, page one: assumptions travel faster than confirmation and arrive dead wrong.
A merchant skipped the checkpoint queue once. Once. The paperwork he generated is still taught as a horror story.
positive: Friendly advisory, friend: a scout skipped one comm check to save time. One. We drill her rescue as a lesson now. Check in.
Story with a moral: the sector that never drilled its worst case met its worst case. Rehearse the ugly stuff. That's the tale.

negative: A tale: a jackal drank at our well nightly, sure of its speed. The well is still there. The speed is a rumor now.
There was a man who mistook the desert's silence for absence. He is part of the silence now.
Listen: a scorpion asked a fire for warmth twice. There is no third asking. This story has room for one more character.
neutral: A traveler once mocked the old paths and took the straight road. The straight road is straight because nothing survives to bend it.
They tell of a rich man who bought a map of our wells. Accurate the day it sold. Wells move. Sellers don't say.
positive: A kind warning wrapped in a story, friend: even the guest of honor checks his boots in the morning. Every morning.
Old tale: the sparrow that fed with falcons grew bold with everyone else. Be bold here, be careful everywhere else.

negative: You want confessions? Earn ears first.
My secrets are for the line. You are not the line.
neutral: Some things I only say to the stove. The stove doesn't repeat and neither do I.
Ask me again when we've shared a bad week. Words like that need mud under them.
positive: Between us and the mud: I still can't sleep before a push. Fourteen years. I fold and refold my blanket like my mother did.
Don't repeat this, friend: I write letters to my village and never send them. A full crate now. The writing holds me together.
You I'll tell: I froze solid my first fight. Osip stepped in front of me like it was nothing. Everything since repays that.
devoted: Listen. When I go, my coat button goes to my daughter. I'm asking you to carry it. Now you know my whole will, friend.
You're on the short list I count as ours. There are five names. Two are dead. Guard yourself.

negative: Personal disclosures require trust. Insufficient balance. Denied.
You're fishing for soft spots. Professionals notice.
neutral: That would be off the record, and I do not speak off the record.
I keep the personal file thin on purpose. Thin files survive.
positive: Between us: I'm sick before every operation. Every one. Then the checklist starts and I'm fine. That's why I love the checklist.
Don't log this anywhere: I nearly resigned in year two. Stayed for my squad. Command thinks it was the pension. Let them.
Here's a real one, friend: I can't recall my mother's voice anymore, but I remember every dead comrade's. What do I do with that?
devoted: I'd put myself between you and a breach without orders. Don't quote me — that's insubordination — but know it.
My personal cipher, friend — the one for family traffic. Learn it. If the towers ever go silent, listen for me on it.

negative: You dig for my soft places with a borrowed shovel. The desert sees the borrowing.
Secrets are water. Yours leak. Mine will not join them.
neutral: The heart is a deep well with a guarded rope. Today the rope stays coiled.
Some truths I tell only to the night wind. You are not the night wind. No offense — it is a high post.
positive: For your ears and the sand's: I fear the open sky. A desert man, afraid of sky. I became a night fighter to hide from noon.
A confidence, friend: I still pray in my mother's dialect, wrong words and all. The old prayers fit my mouth better.
Only you and the fire hear this: I once let an enemy walk away because he sang my village's lullaby. The desert forgave me. Slowly.
devoted: I have told the desert you are mine to protect. It listens to me. Walk anywhere.
If ever you are lost in the dunes, sing that same lullaby. Someone will come. We have arranged it, friend.

negative: Which scar? Some are from people who asked too many questions. Old joke. Half joke.
My scars are receipts. Don't make me itemize yours.
neutral: This one? Wire, winter, hurry. Pick any two and you get a scar like this.
Splinters from the bridge. The bridge lost worse. We're even.
Dog bite, actually. Our dog. The war makes everyone jumpy.
positive: Ha, this beauty? Sled accident. SLED. Survived three offensives and got carved by a hill and a dare. Tell no one.
This one on the arm — I punched through ice to pull Marta out. She hits harder than the ice, by the way. Different story.
The eyebrow? Osip's elbow, celebrating too hard when the relief column arrived. Best scar I own. It's a happy scar.

negative: Injury records are restricted. Causes doubly so. Some causes resemble your associates.
My scars are debriefed, filed, and none of your business.
neutral: Training accident, rope tower. The tower got a redesign, I got a stripe of humility. Fair exchange.
Perimeter breach, year three. The scar is the shape of my own mistake. I keep it visible on purpose.
Burn from signal compounds. Handling procedures exist because of arms like mine.
positive: This one, friend? Shielded a mapcase with my forearm in an ambush. The maps got twelve people home. Best trade my skin made.
The knee? Jumped from the tower during the flood to catch a drowning kid. Doctrine says never jump. The kid disagrees. So do I.
This little one's from my niece's wooden fort. Collapsed on me during 'inspection'. My most honest engineering review to date.

negative: Each scar is a name. Recite them? Some names bite the tongue that says them.
The marked ask the marked carefully. You are asking carelessly.
neutral: Thorn fence, moonless night, borrowed goats. The rest of the story belongs to the goats.
A blade at the pass. The one who gave it carries one of mine. The ledger rests.
Sun-cracked skin from the glass flats. The desert signs its favorites. Roughly.
positive: This crescent? A hawk I raised from a chick, the day she chose the wild. A good scar, friend. Doors should mark you closing.
The long one is from carrying my brother over the salt. He lived. When it aches in cold, I visit and complain. He laughs.
Ah, this? I fell out of the fig tree in my mother's courtyard — last month, on leave. Warrior of the dunes, defeated by breakfast.

negative: Done listening? Good. Doors work both ways. Use yours.
Story time's over. Walk while the mood holds.
neutral: That's all the telling for today. The trench doesn't dig itself.
Enough words. Words don't fill sandbags.
positive: Go on then, friend. Come back for the chapter about the goat.
The rest costs vodka. Fair price. Off you go, then.

negative: This concludes the courtesy. Exit's marked.
End of transmission. Don't make me repeat it.
neutral: That's the releasable portion. Safe travels.
Story's filed. So are you. Move along politely.
positive: Next installment after my rotation, friend. Hold my place.
Copy. Come find me off shift — the good versions have gestures.

negative: The story ends where your welcome does. Both just did.
Go. Some tales follow the listener home. Walk quickly.
neutral: The teller rests, the tale continues elsewhere. Go well.
Enough. Stories are salt — a little seasons, too much thirsts.
positive: The next story needs a moon. Come back when it's full, friend.
Go gently. I will save the ending for your return. It is a good ending.
